How to start:
1. Put the sensor on your arm.
2. Stop the Abbott app and Juggluco. Only one app can hold a sensor.
3. Hold the top of your phone on the sensor until the scan finishes.
4. Allow Bluetooth if you are asked.
5. Warm-up takes about 60 minutes for a new sensor. A sensor that is already running can send glucose sooner.
Hold the top of your phone flat on the sensor. Do not move until the screen changes.
Stop the Abbott app and Juggluco before you scan. A sensor answers only one app, and the last one to scan takes it over.

A pre-soak uses sensor life — read this first

A Libre 3 starts both its warm-up and its 14 day clock at the moment you scan it. There is no way to start a Libre 3 quietly and begin its life later, so a pre-soak spends real wear time: soak it for 12 hours and you have 13.5 days of use left instead of 14.\n\nYou decide when to promote it. There is no smallest soak time.
You can leave this screen. The pre-soak sensor collects readings for itself and does not feed the loop. Open the Libre 3 status screen to watch it and to promote it.

resources.string: Soak time and reading count are shown for information only. There is no smallest soak time, so you decide when to promote.
No pre-soak readings to draw yet. This chart is kept in memory only, so it starts empty again after AAPS restarts, while the reading count below is kept.

The pre-soak sensor becomes the sensor that feeds the loop, right away. The sensor you wear now is retired: it stops sending glucose to AAPS and this phone forgets it. This cannot be undone.

You can promote a sensor that is still warming up, for example when the sensor you wear has failed. A warming sensor sends no glucose until its warm-up ends, so the loop has no glucose for that time.

A Libre 3 often reads low and jumpy for about the first half day after it was started. A young sensor can therefore feed the loop readings that do not match your real glucose. Check with a finger stick before you trust it, and talk to your care team if you are not sure what to do.
Done. The pre-soak sensor now feeds the loop.
The sensor is promoted, but the old calibration entries could not be ignored. Check a fingerstick before you trust the loop, and calibrate again if those old entries still apply.
The sensor looks promoted, but the promotion did not finish cleanly. Check the Libre 3 status to see which sensor feeds the loop before you trust it.
A step after the exchange failed, and the production sensor identity is missing. This is not a complete success. Open the Libre 3 status and check which sensor is in use.
There is no pre-soak sensor to promote.
The pre-soak sensor could not be promoted. Nothing was changed.
